public_rationale: The exact spending figure remains unverified in the accessible independent evidence. Contemporary coverage repeats it while raising questions about completeness. An inference bill approaching an annual cash-burn forecast does not by itself create an accounting contradiction: cash burn also reflects receipts and other cash flows. Neither the reported amount nor the stronger reconciliation concern can be settled from these records.
limitations: An earlier cash-burn projection is context, not the final annual result.
A source's objection to completeness is not a numerical correction.
Zitron's statement of personal uncertainty is not scored as a separate factual claim.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Zitron cannot reconcile the documents' numbers with reporting that OpenAI will have a $9 billion cash burn in CY2025, given that OpenAI had already spent $8.67 billion on inference alone through Q3 CY2025.

statement.excerpt: I also cannot reconcile these numbers with the reporting that OpenAI will have a cash burn of $9 billion in CY2025. On inference alone, OpenAI has already spent $8.67 billion through Q3 CY2025.
statement.document_title: Exclusive: Here's How Much OpenAI Spends On Inference and Its Revenue Share With Microsoft

from_speaker: cash burn of $9 billion in CY2025
already spent $8.67 billion through Q3 CY2025
our_interpretation: The checkable core is approximately $8.67 billion of Azure inference expenditure from January through September 2025.
The $9 billion figure is a reported annual projection that Zitron questions, not his own forecast.
His personal inability to reconcile figures is not independently testable. Assessing an implied accounting inconsistency requires a cash-flow reconciliation.
Gross inference expenditure and net cash burn are different measures; proximity between the two figures alone establishes no contradiction.
The document-based spending figure is treated as a reported estimate without an asserted accounting standard.
criteria.support_condition: Independent records substantiate approximately $8.67 billion of Azure inference expenditure through September 2025. Any stronger claim of incompatibility also requires a reconciliation showing why the annual cash-burn projection could not accommodate it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records materially refute the $8.67 billion spending figure. A complete cash-flow reconciliation could separately refute the implied incompatibility with the annual projection.
